headline: Maye's three picks open the door as Packers torch Patriots

off.text: Next: Thu, Nov 12 vs Canadiens, 7:00 PM
Next: Sun, Nov 15 vs Lions (Munich), 9:30 AM

storylines: First place in the Atlantic is at stake: Philadelphia is 9–2 and leads the East, half a game ahead of 8–2 Boston.
Tyrese Maxey averages 26.9 points for the 76ers, Joel Embiid 17.9 points and 9.7 rebounds, and LeBron James 6.7 assists.
Boston has won eight of nine, and Paul George scored 27 in Sunday's win at Milwaukee.
celtics.edge: Boston: it outscores opponents by 10.7 points a game to Philadelphia's 3.1, and its 15.6 made threes a game rank second in the NBA.

results.headline: Maye's three picks open the door as Packers torch Patriots
results.takeaway: Drake Maye threw three first-half interceptions, the first on his opening pass, and Green Bay piled up 478 yards in a 45–27 rout at Gillette. It's the most points New England has allowed in a regular-season game since 1993.

sections.label: 1st quarter
sections.text: Xavier McKinney intercepted Maye's first pass and returned it to the New England 14, and two plays later Jordan Love scrambled in from 13 yards for a 7–0 lead. Love hit Matthew Golden for a 5-yard touchdown at 7:59 to make it 14–0. Green Bay lost Josh Jacobs (broken finger) and Ty'Ron Hopper (chest) in the quarter.

sections.label: 2nd quarter
sections.text: Trey Smack's 41-yard field goal made it 17–0 before Maye found Rhamondre Stevenson on a 30-yard touchdown. Maye threw two more interceptions in the quarter, and Kaleb Johnson's 2-yard run made it 24–7 before Efton Chism III caught an 8-yard touchdown with 2:37 left. Carlton Davis III and Ben Brown left with knee injuries.

sections.label: 3rd quarter
sections.text: Green Bay scored 18 straight: Love to Savion Williams for 10 yards (31–14), a 51-yard Smack field goal (34–14), then a 39-yard Love strike to Christian Watson after Isaiah McDuffie forced a Stevenson fumble, with Love running in the two-point try for 42–14. Stevenson left with a knee injury, and Maye hit Mack Hollins for a 22-yard score with 1:11 left.

sections.label: 4th quarter
sections.text: Smack added a 38-yard field goal for 45–21, and Corey Kiner ran in from 4 yards with 3:54 left; the two-point try failed. Will Campbell left with a knee injury.

performers.name: Drake Maye
performers.note: All three interceptions came before halftime, and he is now tied for the NFL lead with 11; he said he 'wasn't good today.'

performers.name: DeMario Douglas
performers.note: Led the team in catches and posted the second 100-yard game of his career.

performers.name: Corey Kiner
performers.note: Took over the backfield after Stevenson's knee injury, with TreVeyon Henderson already out ill.

results.oppLine: Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another; Christian Watson had 171 receiving yards and Matthew Golden 164, each with a touchdown.

results.headline: Swayman stops 40 as Bruins win a brawl for four straight
results.takeaway: Elias Lindholm, Mikey Eyssimont and Morgan Geekie scored in the first period and Jeremy Swayman made a season-high 40 saves in a fight-filled 4–1 win. The Bruins have won four straight and lead the Atlantic with 27 points.

sections.label: 1st period
sections.text: Nikita Zadorov fought Brady Tkachuk off the opening faceoff. Lindholm's shot off Jacob Markstrom at 4:50 was ruled no goal, then counted on review, and Eyssimont poked in a loose puck at 6:11 in his season debut for 2–0. Geekie's one-timer on a 5-on-3 made it 3–0, his goal in a fourth straight game, before Carter Verhaeghe scored on a power play. Swayman made 17 saves in the period.

sections.label: 2nd period
sections.text: No goals. Charlie McAvoy was checked for a concussion after a late hit but was cleared for the third. Four 10-minute misconducts were handed out in eight seconds at the end of the period, including to Zadorov and Hampus Lindholm, leaving Boston with four defensemen for half the third.

sections.label: 3rd period
sections.text: JJ Peterka scored 58 seconds in, set up by David Pastrnak, for 4–1. The game finished with 126 penalty minutes and seven misconducts.

performers.name: Jeremy Swayman
performers.note: A season high in saves, 17 of them in the first period, and 12-for-12 on high-danger shots.

performers.name: Mikey Eyssimont
performers.note: Called up from Providence after James Hagens went on IR, he scored 6:11 into his season debut.

performers.name: Morgan Geekie
performers.note: His 5-on-3 one-timer made it 3–0 and extended his goal streak to four games.

results.oppLine: Carter Verhaeghe scored Florida's only goal on a first-period power play, set up by Brady Tkachuk; Jacob Markstrom made 32 saves.

results.headline: George scores 27 as an 18–0 run buries Milwaukee
results.takeaway: Down 27–15 early, Boston answered with an 18–0 run led by Jayson Tatum and Paul George, and George finished with 27 in a 117–97 win. The Celtics have won eight of nine and beat Milwaukee twice in five days.

sections.label: 1st quarter
sections.text: Kyle Kuzma scored 14 points in the first five minutes, hitting 4 of 5 threes, and Milwaukee led 20–6. His basket with 4:17 left made it 27–15, and the Bucks didn't score again in the quarter. Mitchell Robinson came in for Neemias Queta and Tatum made 4 of 6 threes in the quarter.

sections.label: 2nd quarter
sections.text: The run reached 18–0 for a 33–27 lead as Milwaukee went 6:29 without a point. George scored 16 on 6-of-9 shooting in the quarter, his best stretch since the opener.

sections.label: 3rd quarter
sections.text: Mike Conley's three made it 70–47. Robinson made three straight shots, and Sam Hauser's runner at the buzzer ended the quarter.

sections.label: 4th quarter
sections.text: Payton Pritchard hit three straight threes to open the quarter, and Tatum sat the whole fourth.

performers.name: Paul George
performers.note: Scored 16 in the second quarter as Boston turned a 12-point hole into a 13-point halftime lead.

performers.name: Jayson Tatum
performers.note: Made four threes in the first quarter to start the comeback, though he shot 6-of-19, and rested the entire fourth.

performers.name: Mitchell Robinson
performers.note: Listed as questionable with an illness, he had his best game of the season off the bench and was plus-19.

results.oppLine: Kyle Kuzma had 27 points with six threes, 14 of them in the first five minutes; Tyler Herro and Brayden Burries added 13 each.

patriots.headline: Stevenson, Davis and Ben Brown hurt knees
patriots.summary: Rhamondre Stevenson left with a knee injury with 3:29 left in the third quarter, and cornerback Carlton Davis III and guard Ben Brown also left with knee injuries. Left tackle Will Campbell said he would have returned if the score had been closer.

patriots.headline: Maye: 'Just disappointed in myself'
patriots.summary: Drake Maye threw all three of his interceptions before halftime and said he 'put the team in a hole, straight off the bat.' He is tied with Justin Herbert for the NFL lead with 11 interceptions.

patriots.headline: Patriots fly to Munich Wednesday for the Lions
patriots.summary: New England leaves Wednesday night, practices in Germany on Thursday and Friday, and plays Detroit in Munich on Sunday. Vrabel: 'When your best players don't play well, you don't have much of a chance in this league.'

patriots.headline: 45 points, most allowed since 1993
patriots.summary: Green Bay's 45 points were the most the Patriots have allowed in a regular-season game since a 45–7 loss to the Jets on Sept. 26, 1993. The Packers had 478 yards and scored 21 points off four turnovers.

patriots.headline: Gonzalez: 'I had a bad game'
patriots.summary: Christian Gonzalez allowed a career-high 10 catches for 187 yards and a touchdown in his coverage. 'I'm not shaken up by it,' he said.

patriots.headline: Hollins scores in his return from IR
patriots.summary: Mack Hollins played 42 snaps in his first game after four weeks on injured reserve and caught three passes for 36 yards and a touchdown. DeMario Douglas had his second career 100-yard game.

patriots.headline: Henderson reveals hospitalization for neurological symptoms
patriots.summary: TreVeyon Henderson said on Instagram that unexplained neurological symptoms put him in the hospital for several days and have affected his strength and coordination. Testing was reassuring but the cause is unknown; there is no timetable for his return.

patriots.headline: Gronkowski inducted into Patriots Hall of Fame
patriots.summary: Rob Gronkowski was inducted Saturday at a ceremony outside Gillette Stadium, with Tom Brady beside him on stage. "New England will always be home, and I will always love you guys," Gronkowski said. He'll be recognized again at halftime Sunday.

patriots.headline: Marcus Bryant activated; Vildor released
patriots.summary: The Patriots activated tackle Marcus Bryant from injured reserve, where he had been since Aug. 30, and released cornerback Kindle Vildor. They also signed linebacker Elias Neal to the practice squad and released WR Cameron Dorner and OL Jake Kubas from it.

patriots.headline: Trade deadline is Nov. 10
patriots.summary: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. Asked about trade talks, Vrabel said there are "lots of conversations" and "we'll try to do what we can to make the team better."

bruins.headline: Hagens out a few weeks after a crosscheck
bruins.summary: James Hagens went on injured reserve after a crosscheck to the back on Thursday and is expected to miss a few weeks. Mikey Eyssimont, recalled from Providence, scored in his season debut against Florida.

bruins.headline: McAvoy cleared after concussion check
bruins.summary: Charlie McAvoy was taken for a concussion evaluation after a late second-period hit Sunday but was cleared and returned for the third period.

bruins.headline: Swayman and DiPietro: the NHL's best tandem
bruins.summary: Per MoneyPuck, Jeremy Swayman and Mikey DiPietro have combined for 14.8 goals saved above expected, the best in the league. Swayman's 40 saves Sunday were a season high. Sturm: 'They've been awesome.'

bruins.headline: 126 penalty minutes and seven misconducts
bruins.summary: Sunday's game had two first-period fights, seven misconducts and 126 penalty minutes; four 10-minute misconducts came in eight seconds at the end of the second. Sturm on his team's response: 'It was great.'

bruins.headline: Geekie scores in four straight
bruins.summary: Morgan Geekie's 5-on-3 goal Sunday was his fourth straight game with a goal. He has at least five shot attempts in five of his last six games.

bruins.headline: Lindholm on a four-game point streak
bruins.summary: Elias Lindholm has three goals in a four-game point streak and 15 points this season, second on the team behind David Pastrnak. He won 22 of 32 faceoffs against Florida.

bruins.headline: Eyssimont plays with a face shield
bruins.summary: Eyssimont, 30, led the AHL with 13 goals in eight games, including a hat trick Friday. He lost five and a half teeth to a puck last week and wore a face shield Sunday.

bruins.headline: Ten of the next 11 at TD Garden
bruins.summary: Boston opens a four-game homestand Sunday against Florida, followed by Montreal, Minnesota and Los Angeles. The Bruins play 10 of their next 11 games at home and have won 10 of their last 13.

bruins.headline: Bergeron's Hall of Fame weekend; Marchand writes tribute
bruins.summary: Patrice Bergeron is inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame this weekend, and Brad Marchand wrote a testimonial for NHL.com on their years together in Boston.

bruins.headline: Best at 5-on-5 in the NHL
bruins.summary: All six goals in Pittsburgh came at even strength, a season high, and Boston is plus-22 at 5-on-5, the league's best. "Every line can score and every line can be out there in any time of the game," Sturm said.

celtics.headline: Robinson has his best game of the season
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson, listed as questionable with an illness, went 6-of-6 for 12 points with 7 rebounds and 4 steals off the bench in Milwaukee.

celtics.headline: Conley starts in place of Walsh
celtics.summary: Mike Conley started Sunday instead of Jordan Walsh and played 10 minutes, the latest change to Boston's starting lineup.

celtics.headline: Hauser hasn't turned it over all season
celtics.summary: Sam Hauser had played a league-best 186 minutes, 37 seconds without a turnover entering Sunday, and Boston's +18.6 net differential with him on the floor is the best among Celtics players.

celtics.headline: Tatum sits the fourth after 21
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum scored 21 with five threes and sat the entire fourth quarter of the 20-point win, as Boston improved to 8–2 ahead of Tuesday's visit to first-place Philadelphia.

celtics.headline: Celtics set NBA Cup record with 24 threes
celtics.summary: Boston went 24-of-44 from three in Friday's 119–80 win in Charlotte, an NBA Cup record. Its 17 threes in the first half tied a franchise record for a half.

celtics.headline: Boston 2–0 in Cup play at plus-53
celtics.summary: The Celtics have outscored their first two NBA Cup opponents by 53 points, and point differential is a group-play tiebreaker. They have two Cup games left and can still win East Group C or claim a wild card.

celtics.headline: Pritchard cleared, scores 12 off the bench
celtics.summary: Payton Pritchard was cleared to play after his right-eye abrasion and scored 12 points off the bench in Charlotte, including threes in the first and fourth quarters. Devin Carter (illness) was out.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla: Tatum's defense 'sets a different standard'
celtics.summary: Joe Mazzulla praised Jayson Tatum's shot selection in Charlotte but was more impressed by his third-quarter defense. "His competing at the defensive end sets a different standard that we have to have for him," Mazzulla said.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla: 'We need the best version' of George
celtics.summary: Paul George's 25 points against Milwaukee were his most since the season opener. "We need the best version of him for us to be a great team," Mazzulla said.

celtics.headline: Tatum named East Player of the Week
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum won his 14th career Eastern Conference Player of the Week award after averaging 30.3 points, 5.8 rebounds and 7 assists in a 4-0 week, including a career-high 22 free-throw attempts and a buzzer-beater against Brooklyn.

redsox.headline: Dana LeVangie leaves after 35 years
redsox.summary: Dana LeVangie, who was a scout, bullpen coach and pitching coach in a 35-year run with the organization, is leaving and is expected to join the Royals as a scout, per the Boston Globe's Alex Speier.

redsox.headline: GM Meetings open in Las Vegas ahead of lockout
redsox.summary: MLB's General Managers Meetings start Monday in Las Vegas. The labor agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, when the league is set to lock out players and freeze transactions.

redsox.headline: Breslow: front office help 'near or at the top of my list'
redsox.summary: Craig Breslow said Boston hasn't made front office hires yet after assistant GM Taylor Smith left for the Athletics. Dan Meyer was promoted to vice president of baseball research.

redsox.headline: Zack Kelly released after clearing waivers
redsox.summary: Reliever Zack Kelly, designated for assignment in early November, cleared waivers and was released. He is recovering from an elbow fracture.

redsox.headline: Contreras, Abreu named Silver Slugger finalists
redsox.summary: Willson Contreras is an American League finalist at first base and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. The two combined for 51 home runs and were Boston's top two in homers and RBIs. Winners are announced Nov. 17.

redsox.headline: Breslow: Red Sox 'operating under the status quo'
redsox.summary: Ahead of the GM meetings in Las Vegas, Craig Breslow said the lockout uncertainty won't change Boston's approach. The bullpen is coming back intact, and he named more offense and pitching depth as priorities.

redsox.headline: Red Sox add Shelley Duncan to coaching staff
redsox.summary: Boston hired Shelley Duncan, who managed the Yankees' Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre affiliate and was the 2025 International League Manager of the Year. His role isn't set; the Red Sox have openings at first- and third-base coach.

redsox.headline: Tomas Nido elects free agency
redsox.summary: Catcher Tomas Nido elected free agency. He didn't play in the majors for Boston this year, hitting .158 in 10 games at Triple-A Worcester after signing a minor league deal.

redsox.headline: Rafaela, Abreu, Durbin win Gold Gloves
redsox.summary: Ceddanne Rafaela won his second straight Gold Glove in center field and Wilyer Abreu his third straight in right, and Caleb Durbin became the first Red Sox infielder to win one since Ian Kinsler in 2018. It's the first time since 2018 that three Red Sox have won Gold Gloves.

redsox.headline: Red Sox exercise Whitlock's $8.25 million option
redsox.summary: Boston picked up Garrett Whitlock's 2027 club option instead of a $1 million buyout. He had a 1.72 ERA in 54 appearances with 26 holds and pitched through a fractured tibia over the final month; no surgery was needed and he's expected to be ready for spring training.

nba.cutNote: Top 6 make the playoffs, 7–10 the play-in

nhl.cutNote: Top 3 in each division plus 2 wild cards make the playoffs

nfl.cutNote: Top 7 make the playoffs (division winners seeded 1–4)
